source_evidence.observation: The source says that a random variable is centered by subtracting its mean and introduces the displayed formula as a simple centering inequality for the L2 norm.
The displayed claim is ||X - E X||_{L2} <= ||X||_{L2}.
The source next announces a similar inequality for the sub-gaussian norm, distinguishing Equation (2.19) itself as the L2 inequality.

binders: X, the random variable appearing in the displayed inequality; the source does not explicitly quantify X or name its probability space here [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
conclusions: The L2 norm of the centered random variable is no greater than the L2 norm of the original random variable: ||X - E X||_{L2} <= ||X||_{L2} [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
definitions_and_conventions: Centering a random variable means subtracting its mean, so the centered variable is X - E X [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 opening paragraph and Equation (2.19)].
E X denotes the mean/expectation of X, as indicated by the phrase "subtracting the mean" immediately before the formula [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 opening paragraph].
The notation ||.||_{L2} is used for the L2 norm; no further definition of that notation is given in the cited passage [PDF page 19; printed page 30, lead-in to Equation (2.19) and Equation (2.19)].
implicit_context: The expectation and both L2 norms must be meaningful; the cited passage leaves the precise integrability convention implicit [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].

The statement is made in a section about centering random variables, not as a deterministic inequality for arbitrary normed-space elements [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 heading and opening paragraph].

details: The transformed variable is obtained by subtracting its own expectation, X - E X [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 opening paragraph and Equation (2.19)].
Both sides use the L2 norm, and the comparison direction is <= [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
The bound has exact multiplicative constant 1 [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].

Equation (2.19) is the L2 centering inequality; the sub-gaussian-norm centering statement is introduced only afterward as a similar result [PDF page 19; printed page 30, sentence after Equation (2.19) and Lemma 2.6.8].

undebatable_constraints: The left-hand side must be the L2 norm of X - E X [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
The right-hand side must be the L2 norm of X itself [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
The relation is an upper bound, ||X - E X||_{L2} <= ||X||_{L2}, with constant 1 [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19)].
Equation (2.19) does not state the later psi_2 bound with an unspecified absolute constant C [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Equation (2.19) and Lemma 2.6.8 immediately below].

ambiguities.issue: The display does not explicitly quantify X or state its codomain and integrability hypotheses.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.19) writes the inequality directly after referring generically to centering a random variable; no binder or hypothesis accompanies the display [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 opening paragraph and Equation (2.19)].
ambiguities.impact: A formal version must choose a probability space, a scalar codomain, and assumptions or conventions ensuring E X and the L2 norms are defined; these choices should not add substantive restrictions beyond what is needed to express the source inequality.

ambiguities.issue: The cited passage uses L2 notation without restating its definition.
ambiguities.evidence: The lead-in calls (2.19) an inequality for the L2 norm, and the display uses ||.||_{L2}, but the cited page supplies no definition of that norm [PDF page 19; printed page 30, lead-in to Equation (2.19) and Equation (2.19)].
ambiguities.impact: Comparison with a formal target must verify that its L2 notion is the standard probability-space L2 norm intended by the source rather than a differently normalized or unrelated norm.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For the random variable X in the centering discussion, subtracting its expectation cannot increase its L2 norm: ||X - E X||_{L2} <= ||X||_{L2}. The displayed bound uses constant 1 and is specifically an L2 statement; the separate sub-gaussian centering bound comes afterward [PDF page 19; printed page 30, Section 2.6.1 opening paragraph, Equation (2.19), and the sentence immediately following it].
